analysis.title: Tug of war between resilient macro and risk off
key_insights: US Treasuries closed with a modest bull-steepening on 17 Nov. The 10Y UST yield closed around 5.10%, about 3bp lower on the day, after hawkish data pushed yields up early and a late risk-off bid reversed the move.
October US retail sales rose 0.2% m/m, slowing from 0.8% in September but above expectations. Ex-autos sales rose 0.6% (exp. 0.4%), and ex-autos and gas rose 0.5%. September figures were revised up.

The S&P 500 fell for a fourth straight session and touched its lowest level since June (the report also says July). Every major global index closed lower. Euro Stoxx 50 and DAX fell 2.1% and FTSE 100 fell 1.8%.
Tech led the selloff on both sides of the Atlantic on pre-Nvidia earnings nerves and reports that the NSA's classified internal communications network went down.

Nvidia reported Q3 revenue of $115.8bn, up 103% y/y and 6.3% above the $109.3bn consensus. Adjusted EPS was $2.68 against $2.47 expected. Q4 revenue guidance is $130bn (±3%) and FY28 growth guidance was raised to 75% from 70%. Shares rose 4.7% after hours, after falling more than 35% from the 6 October peak.
Nvidia's board will not reinstate former CEO Jensen Huang and is searching for a replacement. Interim CEO Colette Kress said demand is 'far exceeding supply'.
The 10Y OAT-Bund spread tightened by more than 6bp after the RN unveiled a pension reform proposal that the market received relatively positively.
Credit indices widened on Tuesday: Main +1.4bp, Crossover +7bp, CDX IG +1.2bp. Automotive CDS widened with oil. Nvidia CDS tightened 3.6bp ahead of results.

Deutsche Bank fell 6% after a media consortium published findings from over 15 million leaked internal documents alleging compliance failures, accounting irregularities and misleading disclosures, including $582mn of suspicious payments linked to Jeffrey Epstein. Natixis rates the news credit negative for DB.
UBS is reportedly resigned to tighter capital requirements, is revisiting a possible headquarters move abroad, and is exploring small and mid-sized US acquisitions.

Natixis frames the near-term tension in US markets as resilient growth and sticky inflation pushing yields higher, against Persian Gulf geopolitical risk and AI-linked cyber uncertainty producing safe-haven demand that flattens the curve.

market_movers.rationale: Q3 revenue and EPS beat, Q4 guidance of $130bn and FY28 growth guidance raised to 75%. Shares rose 4.7% after hours. The board declined to reinstate Jensen Huang and is searching for a CEO.
Shares fell 6% after a leak of over 15 million internal documents. Natixis rates it credit negative. DB defends the matters as nearly two decades old and already addressed with regulators.

sector_views.rationale: Tech led the global selloff on pre-Nvidia nerves and the NSA network outage report, while Nvidia's results and guidance beat expectations.

earnings_insights: Nvidia Q3 FY27 (reported 17 Nov after the close): revenue $115.8bn, up 103% y/y, versus consensus $109.3bn. Adjusted EPS $2.68 versus consensus $2.47. Q4 FY27 revenue guidance $130bn (±3%).
Nvidia FY28 growth guidance is now 75%, up from 70%.

Loxam Q3-26 (BB-/NR) results were moderately positive: revenue and EBITDA grew and international operations held up against weakness in France. Margins contracted, free cash flow was negative and net debt rose since year-end.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Slower than September's +0.8% but above expectations. Supports the higher-for-longer narrative.

geopolitical: Persian Gulf geopolitical risk is generating episodic safe-haven demand.
RN, the far-right party leading polls for the French presidential election, unveiled a pension reform proposal.
US-China AI truce: a Natixis Asia research title says the Nvidia episode leaves it 'without a defender'.
